newsitem.title: ESTONIA: HANSA AND FOREKSPANK LEAD STRONG MARKET RALLY.
newsitem.headline: HANSA AND FOREKSPANK LEAD STRONG MARKET RALLY.

text.p: * Total trade was 102.5 million kroons on Tuesday compared
to 77.2 million kroons on Monday.
* Talse gained 1.68 percent to close on 271.51.
* Hansapank and Forekspank dominated
trade with Hansapank turning over 36.9 milliion kroons to be 2.2
kroons higher on 145.1.
* Forekspank saw 20.5 million kroons traded to be 7.50
kroons higher on 191 kroons.
* On the free market, Norma traded 14.1 million
kroons to close 1.4 kroons higher at 74.5 kroons.
(A complete report follows)
(See index on stock exchange web site:
http://www.tse.ee/online/total.htm)
Share prices rallied again on
the Estonian bourse on Tuesday with Hansapank and Forekspank
leading the charge on the main list.
The Talse index rose 1.68 percent to 271.51 with 86.1
million kroons traded on the main list.
The market has been riding the crest of a wave of interest
that began last week amid talk of bank mergers and expectations
for bank 1997 profit forecast increases.
Forekspank's share price rose by four percent or by 7.5
kroons to close on 191 kroons on trade of 20.5 million kroons.
"Forekspank is a cheap stock, even with its higher price,
and this was the main interest in it," one trader said.
"Foreskspank is still cheaper than Hansa and Hoiu
and it made most price gains in today's trade," one trader said.
Some dealers expected more calm to return to the market.
"As for tomorrow, the volume will be less, but prices should
also rise slightly tomorrow, with more smaller investors
active," another dealer said.
Hansapank was most active stock on healthy trade of 36.9
million kroons to gain 2.2 kroons for a close on 145.10 kroons.
"Despite Hansapank's price, it is still an active blue chip
that attracts institutional interest," another trader said.
Trade on the free market was 16.1 million kroons with Norma
completely dominating on 14 million kroons.
Norma is still being boosted by a five month report that saw
profits gain 1.40 kroons to 74.50 kroons.
-- David Mardiste, Tallinn newsroom, +372 620 9202/1,
reuters@reuters.ee
